title: THE BLESSEDNESS OF THE RIGHTEOUS
mv: The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
mvp: “The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.” Psalm 92:12 (NKJV)
outline: The Condition For Divine Blessings And Its Results
assignment: Identify five (5) people the Bible calls “righteous” with one scriptural reference each to support your answer (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Psalm one stands as a kind of introduction to the rest of the Psalms. Its subject matter touches on two themes: the blessedness of the righteous and the doom of the ungodly. In this lesson, we shall do an exposition on Psalm 1:1-3, which deals with the character of the righteous and the conditions for divine blessings.

The Psalmist begins with the character of a godly man in verse one: “Blessed is the man Who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, Nor stands in the path of sinners, Nor sits in the seat of the scornful.”

To be blessed means to be highly favoured by divine grace and to enjoy the bliss of heaven. Firstly, ‘the man’ receives the blessings of God because he does not ‘walk in the counsel of the ungodly.’ The counsels of the ungodly are advice and plans that do not conform to God’s word (Proverbs 1:10; 2 Samuel 13:3-5, 14). ‘The ungodly’ live or act without the consciousness of God. Therefore, ‘the man’ (a believer in Christ) who will enjoy the blessings of God must not embrace ungodly principles or practices (Ephesians 5:11; Proverbs 24:1).

Secondly, ‘the man’ does not stand in the ways of sinners (Proverbs 1:11-15; 4:14-17). That is, he does not compromise, or submit to the position of sinners (Daniel 3:16-18). Therefore, ‘the man’ (a believer in Christ) who will enjoy the blessings of God must be firm in his faith and flee from every appearance of evil (2 Timothy 2:19; 1 Thessalonians 5:22).

Thirdly, ‘the man’ does not sit in the seat of the scornful. The scornful are those who mock the heavens or anything that represents God. They openly defy all that is sacred, and make a jest of sin (Exodus 5:2; 2 Chronicles 32:10-15). Scorners are un-teachable because they refuse to listen (Proverbs 9:8a; 15:12). Therefore, the man that will be blessed does not mingle with these people.

Psalm 1:1 therefore implies that sin is progressive, i.e. one evil act leads to another; He who acts by bad counsel may soon do evil deeds, and he who gives himself to evil doings may end up in apostasy (James 1:14-15).

sections.h: THE CONDITION FOR DIVINE BLESSINGS AND ITS RESULTS

b.x: The condition for being blessed is stated in Psalm 1:2, and it means the man’s will, desire, affection, motives, and every principle in his soul are on the side of God and His truth. He takes up the law of the Lord (God’s word) as the rule of his life (Psalm 119:1, 97; James 1:25). To meditate on God’s word is to discourse with oneself concerning the great things contained in it, with a close application of mind. This must continue until the word becomes a reality in his life (Joshua 1:8; Psalm 119:11).

The result of the fulfilment of the condition for being blessed is found in Psalm 1:3. A man planted by the rivers of water is likened to a man who has a regular supply of nourishment and refreshments. He experiences irreversible fruitfulness and will not suffer loss of any kind (Jeremiah 17:7-8). He will be healthy all-round, prosperous and enjoy the fruit of his labour (Psalm 92:12-14).
To remain blessed; abstain from every appearance of evil and live by the word of God.
